name: Netplay
description: Shared-screen netplay and link-cable play between two handhelds, over an ad hoc network the devices create themselves.
author: bmpriest

changelog.v3.2.5-cable: Stops believing single writes to the USB controller, and marks H700 experimental. Three changes, all the same idea: a controller attribute is offered repeatedly and read back rather than written once and trusted, because on this vendor kernel the failing attempt is itself harmful. The daemon's bind now retries for up to five seconds and logs the tick count when it takes more than one; the app's own startup repair does the same for both the release and the bind, where it previously tried once and gave up; and both rebuild paths now wait for the functionfs instance's endpoint files to appear before offering the controller at all, since writing it before the instance is presentable is what produced failed to start g1: -19. Those markers are now gone from every captured session cycle. They were not the whole story: H700 still freezes after a couple of cable sessions because the gadget takeover itself - creating and destroying configfs/functionfs objects - corrupts this vendor kernel's heap, which shows up as a slab fault in an unrelated subsystem each time (kernfs_fop_open, a mali mmap, an Ion CMA allocation). So H700 is now labelled experimental in the README and this changelog, with what a freeze looks like, the two power-cycles it takes to come back, the dirty-card follow-up, and the two candidate fixes (hold one takeover for the whole boot, or link this pak's function alongside the firmware's instead of swapping). tg5040 is unaffected by any of it. tg5040 + h700 build.
changelog.v3.2.4-cable: mGBA is now used only while a session is armed. The pak's own mGBA build is selected at launch for the life of the session, and the device's mGBA pak is left exactly as it is, instead of being replaced permanently - so ordinary single-player mGBA keeps running whatever the device had. A device with no mGBA pak at all is given the one this build ships, at arm time and only then, because with no pak NextUI sends GBA roms to a different emulator entirely. This works because mGBA is the one core whose netplay build cannot be a shared compatibility artifact: upstream's libretro build does not compile the lockstep SIO drivers at all, so what has to match is this pak's build per platform, and the paired core stays the instanced route. Also hardens taking the firmware's USB gadget over, after a freeze on h700 showed the vendor kernel corrupting its own heap: the controller release is confirmed by reading the attribute back rather than trusting a write that can return ENODEV after it succeeded, the firmware's function is unlinked before its mount comes down, a failed unmount cancels the removal instead of removing a mounted function, our own teardown asks /proc/mounts before removing anything, and a daemon that finds a repair record from an earlier run refuses to build a second takeover on top of it. Adds h700 as a beta platform (Anbernic XX devices on BaseOS): building a cable session there works, and testing was done with the H700 handheld as the gadget end and a Brick as the USB host, but repeated arm/stop cycles have been seen to freeze the device and need a reboot - see the release notes. The H700 port's socket rules differ from the Brick's: those devices have a single USB-C that is both charge and OTG, so there is no host-only top socket to put the cable in.
changelog.v3.2.3-cable: Stops the joining end switching a socket it does not need to switch. It used to force its port to host unconditionally, on the assumption the cable was in the bottom socket; that switch brings up the bottom socket's host controller, and the bottom socket is also the charge socket, so a charger plugged into it was being back-fed with 5 V for the whole session. The top socket is host-only and bound from boot, so when the cable is there the peer can be seen without touching anything. The joining end now looks first and switches only if nothing answers, and if the peer turns out to be reachable through the top socket's controller it gives the socket straight back. Measured on two Bricks with the link up and a game running: the port stays in usb_device mode, the bottom socket's buses never come up, no repair record is written, and the joining end gains battery. tg5040 build only.
changelog.v3.2.2-cable: Cable link fixes, all found by playing over it. An accidental unplug no longer ends the link: the hosting end now waits for the peer to come back instead of exiting, and the joining end's device scan no longer opens USB nodes it has not identified first - opening the wrong one blocked the daemon in uninterruptible sleep, which needed a reboot to clear. The cable's input-delay floor drops from 3 frames to 1, from a measured 0.3-0.7 ms round trip: the old value was borrowed from ad hoc before the cable had ever been measured, and cost about 50 ms of avoidable input lag. tg5040 build only.
changelog.v3.2.1-cable: Fixes the cable link against what the hardware actually does. The daemon no longer creates its own USB gadget - this kernel allows exactly one, and the firmware's already owns it - so it takes the firmware's over for the session and puts its function, mount, userspace and identity back on the way out. The port is switched by reading the vendor's trigger node rather than writing otg_role, which this BSP refuses. A cable session now ends with adb working and the repair record cleared, and the daemon no longer dies mid-restore. Also: a stale pidfile no longer blocks a later launch. tg5040 build only.
changelog.v3.2.0-cable: A third transport: a USB-C cable between two devices. The host presents a userspace FunctionFS gadget and the peer claims the same vendor interface over usbfs; a TUN interface on each end carries the existing TCP transport unchanged. No radio is moved and no WiFi is touched, so the ad-hoc and hotspot paths are unaffected. Adds the link= session key, which also lets a previous build's session file keep working. tg5040 build only.
changelog.v3.1.1-test: Test build for different devices, including dual instance support for gambatte and mgba.
changelog.v2.1.0-test: Instanced link play for Game Boy: both devices emulate both consoles and WiFi carries only controller inputs. Works with two different linked cartridges - Gold/Silver, Seasons/Ages - found inside a zipped library without transferring any game file. Cartridge real-time clocks are negotiated so each console keeps its own owner's time. Verified with a completed Pokemon trade across 13,500 frames with no desync.
changelog.v2.0.0-test: Libretro shim, ad hoc networking, local compatibility-core fallback, bind-mounted pak wrapping, and WiFi recovery. Adds my282, my355 and h700.
